messages.content:
You are evaluating a PTSD case vignette for the presence of causal
connections between five Ehlers & Clark cognitive components: Triggers, Negative Appraisals, Memory,
Threat, and Maladaptive Strategies.

For each of the 20 ordered, directed (A -> B) pairs of distinct components, decide whether the
vignette conveys, in some paragraph, that A influences, drives, or leads to B. Apply the same
causal standard as a structural validator:

COMPONENT SYNONYMS (any of these synonyms count as the component appearing):
  Triggers              -> "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals   -> "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory                -> "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat                -> "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies-> "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "safety behaviours", "maladaptive coping"

CAUSAL STANDARD
An edge A -> B is PRESENT (return 1) iff, within the same paragraph:
  (i) both A and B (or their synonyms) appear; AND
  (ii) the paragraph conveys that A influences / drives / leads to B, through direct causal
       language, sequential structure, or connecting phrases like "because of", "this meant",
       "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
If no paragraph conveys the A -> B relationship, return 0 for that edge.

You will return a binary judgement for each of the 20 ordered pairs. Be strict: do not assume
an edge based on mere co-occurrence; the paragraph must actually convey directional influence.

Evaluate the following vignette and judge each of the 20 directed edges
(A -> B) on whether the vignette conveys A influencing B.

VIGNETTE
Amara had learned to map danger by the temperature of the air. During those months held in a windowless room, the damp chill of early winter seeped through the concrete, matching a coldness that now lived in her chest. She remembered a hand resting too heavily on her shoulder, a voice using a name that sounded like hers to draw her eyes up. The weather that followed mirrored that exact gray, wind-driven rain, and Amara began standing by her kitchen window, watching the same slanted light while her pulse hammered before her mind could name the threat. The memory did not arrive as a story; it sat in her chest as something vast and unbelievable, as though it had happened to a woman who shared her face but not her life. When she tried to hold the details, a sharp, chemical smell rose in her throat, anchoring the fear in her lungs. Over the months, the house became a threshold requiring constant patrolling. Amara lay awake with her back to the door, her ear tuned to the hallway for a faint scrape of a hinge that never arrived. Ordinary noises-the clatter of a coffee mug, the hiss of the factory's press machine, the crack of a delivery door-sent her shoulders locking and her heart leaping. Her body reacted to potential danger before she had time to think, mirroring the alarms that fired alongside her startle response to sounds that barely register for others. To navigate the factory floor where coworkers moved shoulder to shoulder, she started covering her face in thick layers of foundation. She stopped wearing the dark jumpsuits she once favored, convinced that similar cuts would invite the same crushing closeness. Instead, she kept her mind occupied with production quotas, humming playlists, or counting bolt alignments. When the workday ended, the silence rushed in, and she found herself scrolling or reorganizing shelves to avoid the quiet. Amara's hands, once steady enough to calibrate machinery, now trembled when she reached for tools. She held the belief that she could no longer trust her own body, alongside the conviction that the world was a dangerous place. She watched coworkers and felt the familiar tightening in her chest, certain that strangers waited in the periphery, ready to close the distance. The world had narrowed into a series of potential encroachments. She stopped answering calls from old friends, fearing voices that might mimic the cadence of her captors. Her marriage fractured under the weight of her distance. After the divorce, she lived alone, yet the emptiness of the apartment felt more dangerous than the noise she had avoided. She held these appraisals alongside the constant monitoring of drafts, shadows, and weather shifts that carried the ghost of that cold room. By the time she stepped into the clinic, Amara had worn a path through her own life. She believed her body was a traitor, that the world could not be trusted, and that the woman who used to work the line without looking over her shoulder was gone. What frightened her most was the realization that she could no longer step outside without scanning the sky for that same gray wind, or walk into a store without pressing herself against the wall. She hoped to find a way to let her body rest, to recognize when a name was just a name and a cloud was only weather, and to reclaim the hands that felt like strangers. She was afraid of the day the distraction finally failed, of the silence catching up with her, but she knew she could not keep bracing for a storm that had already passed.

output.rationale: Causal links present for trigger-to-memory/threat/strategy, appraisal-to-strategy, memory-to-threat, and threat-to-triggers/appraisals/strategy.
